text: The Falklands (Q9648) are a British Overseas Territory (Q46395).
source_text: As a British Overseas Territory (Q46395) , the Falklands (Q9648) have internal self-governance (Q417633) , while the United Kingdom takes responsibility for their defence and foreign affairs. The capital and largest settlement is Stanley (Q12245) on East Falkland (Q642226). The islands are believed to have been uninhabited prior to European discovery in the 17th century. Controversy exists over the Falklands (Q9648)' discovery and subsequent colonisation by Europeans. At various times, the islands have had French (Q70972), British, Spanish, and Argentine (Q2365041) settlements. Britain reasserted its rule in 1833 , but Argentina (Q414) maintains its claim to the islands.

text: In April 1982, Argentine military forces invaded the islands.

In a 2013 sovereignty referendum (Q2359115) , almost all of the votes cast were in favour of remaining a UK overseas territory. The territory's sovereignty status is part of an ongoing dispute between Argentina (Q414) and the UK . The 2021 census recorded a population of 3,662 inhabitants, around 30% of which are temporary residents, on short-term work visas or working at the RAF Mount Pleasant (Q2071294) military base. English is the official and predominant language.

text: The Falkland Islands (Q9648) Act 1983 is under the British Nationality Act.
source_text: Under the British Nationality (Falkland Islands (Q9648)) Act 1983 , Falkland Islanders (Q3502570) are British citizens (Q918305) . The islands lie at the boundary of the subantarctic oceanic (Q182090) and tundra climate (Q2459798) zones, and both major islands have mountain ranges reaching 2,300 ft (700 m). They are home to large bird populations, although many no longer breed on the main islands owing to predation by introduced species . source_text: Vernet settled at the ruins of Puerto Soledad (Q7258835) in 1826, and accumulated resources on the islands until the venture was secure enough to bring settlers and form a permanent colony. Buenos Aires (Q1486) named Vernet military and civil commander of the islands in 1829, and he attempted to regulate sealing to stop the activities of foreign whalers and sealers. Vernet's venture lasted until a dispute related to fishing and hunting rights led to a raid (Q5431979) by the American warship USS Lexington (Q7871244) in 1831, when United States Navy (Q11220) commander Silas Duncan (Q3294548) declared the dissolution of the island's government.

source_text: Vernet's deputy, the Scotsman Matthew Brisbane (Q6790214) , returned to the islands that year to restore the business, but his efforts ended after, amid unrest at Port Louis (Q3435209), gaucho Antonio Rivero (Q2857426) led a group of dissatisfied individuals to murder Brisbane and the settlement's senior leaders; survivors hid in a cave on a nearby island until the British returned and restored order. In the  late 1830s, an appeal was made to the Colonial Office in London by businessmen seeing potential profit, for organised settlement of the islands. In 1840, the Falklands (Q9648) became a Crown colony (Q1351282) and Scottish settlers subsequently established an official pastoral community.

After the war ended, the Falklands (Q9648) economy was affected by declining wool prices and the political uncertainty resulting from the revived sovereignty dispute between the United Kingdom and Argentina (Q414). Simmering tensions between the UK and Argentina (Q414) increased during the second half of the century, when Argentine President Juan Perón (Q93330) asserted sovereignty over the archipelago (Q33837). The sovereignty dispute intensified during the 1960s, shortly after the United Nations passed a resolution on decolonisation (Q230533) which Argentina (Q414) interpreted as favourable to its position.

text: In April 1982, the Falklands War (Q48249) began.
source_text: In April 1982 the Falklands War (Q48249) began when Argentine (Q2365041) military forces invaded the Falklands (Q9648) and other British territories in the South Atlantic (Q97) , briefly occupying them until a UK expeditionary force (Q11682252) retook the territories in June. After the war the UK expanded its military presence, building RAF Mount Pleasant (Q2071294) and increasing the size of its garrison. The war also left some 117 minefields containing nearly 20,000 mines of various types, including anti-vehicle and anti-personnel mines. Due to the large number of deminer (Q1345044) casualties, initial attempts to clear the mines ceased in 1983.

text: The islands Q5133614 have a cold climate.

Land birds make up most of the Falklands (Q9648)' avifauna (Q5113) . The only endemic (Q123452) bird species on the Falkland Islands (Q9648) are the flightless Falkland (Q1012069) steamer duck and Cobb's wren (Q531002) . Sixty-three species breed on the islands, including 14 endemic (Q123452) subspecies (Q68947) .

text: The abundant arthropod diversity on the islands is associated with the number Q1360.
source_text: Abundant arthropod (Q1360) diversity occurs on the islands. The Falklands (Q9648)' flora consists of 163 native vascular plant (Q27133) species. More than 400 species of lichens (Q43142) and lichen-dwelling fungi (Q3238100) have been recorded. The islands' only native terrestrial mammal, the warrah (Q205935) , was hunted to extinction by European settlers. The islands are frequented by marine mammals (Q382441) , such as the southern elephant seal (Q215343) and the South American fur seal (Q649127) , and various types of cetaceans (Q160) ; offshore islands house the rare striated caracara .

text: The Falk Islands' economic activity increasingly focused on oil field exploration after the end of the Falklands War in 1982.
source_text: Since the end of the Falklands War (Q48249) in 1982, the islands' economic activity increasingly focused on oil field exploration (Q3241434) and tourism. All large settlements are now connected by road and, since 2008, a ferry links West and East Falkland (Q642226). The islands' major exports include wool, hides, venison, fish and squid; its main imports include fuel, building materials (Q206615) and clothing. The port settlement of Stanley (Q12245) has regained the islands' economic focus, with an increase in population as workers migrate from Camp (Q2614518).

text: Fear of dependence on fishing licences led to increased interest in oil drilling as an alternative source of revenue.
source_text: Fear of dependence on fishing licences and threats from overfishing , illegal fishing (Q675637) and fish market price fluctuations (Q1004322) led to increased interest in oil drilling as an alternative source of revenue. As of 2001, exploration (Q3241434) efforts had yet to find "exploitable reserves". By 2023, oil exploration (Q3241434) was still proceeding off the shelf of the islands with a deepwater project led by Rockhopper Exploration (Q7355289) . Development projects in education and sports have been funded by the Falklands (Q9648) government, without aid from the United Kingdom.

text: The Falkland Islands (Q9648) population is homogeneous.
source_text: The Falkland Islands (Q9648) population is homogeneous, mostly descended from Scottish and Welsh immigrants who settled in the territory after 1833, and also from English and French people (Q121842) , Gibraltarians (Q285828) , Scandinavians, and South Americans. The 2016 census indicated that 43% of residents were born in the archipelago (Q33837), with foreign-born residents assimilated into local culture. The legal term for the right of residence is "belonging to the islands". In 1983, full British citizenship (Q918305) was given to Falkland Islanders (Q3502570) under the British Nationality (Falkland Islands (Q9648)) Act 1983 .
